parts:
Alicia,


There are many ways of obtaining species means in R or geomorph.  One way is to use the function ‘mshape’ for each group (see help file). Another is:

 

Y.means <- rowsum(Y, groups)/as.vector(table(groups))

 

Where Y is a two.d.array of aligned coordinates, and groups is a factor for species.

 

I’m sure others will provide additional implementations in their responses.

parts:
Alicia,

Two things. First, it’s a bad idea to call an object the same name as a function. The function, data, and your name of data means R has to discern between the two, which can cause errors. Second, you do not name the data within the data frame. Therefore, it is no longer a set (a matrix) but instead, the variables in the original set are liberated. For example, if you have a matrix of three variables, called “dat”, comprising x, y, and z, in the defining of the data frame, you need to say,

dat = dat 

To not do that - like you did - is tantamount to telling R you want to add x, y, and z, separately. 

Hope that helps. 
Mike

Hi Alicia,

The problem arises from trying to assign names to specimens in a set when there really is no set - just one specimen.   In this case, the data are no longer formatted as an array.  Furthermore, I’m not sure what will happen when one asks to take the mean of one specimen.  We don’t always anticipate these instances because it takes an awkward case to suggest such cases could exist (who would write a function to find the mean of one observation, normally?).

Whether the problem can be solved depends on what you mean by the problem.  Is there an analytical solution?  Sure.  One could figure that out.  Do you mean can we fix the functions to allow sets of 1 or find the mean of one observation?  This is also possible, but I have to warn you that it cannot supersede the updates we are currently making, but possibly become part of them.  Because we are updating functions for the next geomoprh version, we need to also consider how other updates affect multiple functions, so introducing an additional variable will cause some programming issues.  Maybe in a week or two we might be able to consider this, and only if there is a general solution.  (Sometimes peculiar data sets call for unique solutions rather than general ones.  If a solution is not a geomorph issue, but more of an R issue - like changing arrays to matrices or vectors, inherently, then there might be little we can do avoid pitfalls with geomorph and a kluge might be needed for your data.)

Cheers!
Mike
